key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerance gains from biased-noise qubits only become substantial when the available gates and measurements preserve the noise bias; otherwise, the overhead benefit largely disappears.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware, this means the right native operations can turn strongly biased physical noise into a practical path toward lower-overhead error correction and magic-state preparation.
method: Organizes fault-tolerance protocols by the bias-preserving operation set available on the hardware.
Compares the CZ-only setting with a bias-preserving CX setting and a measurement-based alternative.
Links the error hierarchy to code design: dedicated protection for frequent phase flips and concatenation for rare bit flips.
evidence_signal: The review argues, based on protocol analysis and experimentally relevant error rates, that CZ-only architectures lose most of the advantage of noise bias, while CX- or measurement-based architectures can recover substantial overhead reductions.
watch_item: The main implementation risk is that naturally biased platforms often cannot support a true bias-preserving CX, and even engineered platforms may struggle to achieve the required high-fidelity operations or QND multi-qubit Z readout.
paper_title: Biased-noise qubits: a guide to efficient fault-tolerance using the hierarchy of errors
